public_rationale: Ars Technica reports OpenAI's calendar-2025 operating loss as $20.92 billion and its headline net loss as nearly $39 billion [e1]. CTech/Reuters reports Anthropic's 2025 operating loss as $8.06 billion, which rounds to $8 billion [e2]. Both claimed amounts match reported operating losses at the stated precision [e1, e2]. These items do not establish the amounts as a matching pair of net losses on a consistent accounting basis [e1, e2]. The figures therefore support an operating-loss reading but cannot settle the unspecified loss measure [e1, e2].
limitations: The claim does not specify operating loss versus net loss or an accounting basis.
No original OpenAI annual financial statement was retrieved to reconcile consolidated and attributable net losses.
The cited evidence items do not supply Anthropic's 2025 net loss.
The loss figures cannot settle the subjective description of the companies as 'astonishingly bad businesses'.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI and Anthropic lost $20.92 billion and $8 billion respectively in 2025 and are astonishingly bad businesses.

statement.excerpt: Both OpenAI and Anthropic are astonishingly bad businesses, losing $20.92 billion and $8 billion respectively in 2025.

our_interpretation: Assess the financial amounts separately from the subjective judgment about business quality.
Unqualified annual loss ordinarily means net loss, but operating loss is a material alternative reading that must be checked rather than silently substituted.
Use calendar 2025 and US dollars. Treat $8 billion as rounded to the nearest billion and $20.92 billion as rounded to the nearest hundredth of a billion.
The quoted assertion does not specify an accounting basis. Finding numbers that resemble operating losses does not authorize assigning that metric to an unqualified claim.
criteria.support_condition: Independent financial records establish the respective 2025 losses at the stated precision on a specified, matching metric and accounting basis.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Independent records establish different losses beyond the stated rounding tolerances on the same specified metric and accounting basis. Differences between operating and net loss alone cannot settle an unspecified metric.

evidence.explanation: The report separately identifies $20.92 billion as loss from operations and a much larger headline net loss. It establishes why substituting one metric for the other would change the verdict.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Clarification of the claimed loss metric and accounting basis, followed by both companies' calendar-2025 financial statements or independent reporting based on those records. The comparison must distinguish consolidated and attributable losses, identify adjustments, and apply the stated rounding precision. The business-quality judgment remains subjective.
